title: Account Recovery Sprint Blueprint
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, executable blueprint to recover accounts that have entered a high-risk renewal state within the next 90 days. It is intentionally prescriptive: short timeframe, prioritized tactics, and a single owner per action. Use for mid-market and enterprise customers where there is measurable revenue at stake and multiple internal stakeholders.

Scope and when to use:
- Triggers: 30–90 day window to renewal AND one or more of: sudden usage drop of >40% month-over-month, support case backlog >3 open P1/P2s, product/contract concerns raised in last QBR, executive churn on customer side, or NPS decline >15 points in last 60 days.
- Not for churn prevention at scale (use standard lifecycle playbooks) — this is a concentrated sprint for accounts showing clear near-term risk.

Outcome goals (SMART):
- Primary: Convert at-risk renewal to renewed contract (same or expanded ARR) within 60 days.
- Secondary: Resolve top 2 technical blockers, obtain written exec commitment (email) from customer sponsor, and execute a follow-up QBR within 30 days of contract signature.

High-level phases (14–28 day sprint):
1) Triage (48 hours) — data + initial outreach
2) Mitigate (7–10 days) — product fixes, short-term concessions, adoption actions
3) Executive alignment (parallel — within 7 days) — exec-to-exec briefing and decision
4) Close + follow-up (remaining sprint days) — execute contract, transition to success plan

Roles & RACI (one-line):
- Owner (R): Customer Success Manager (CSM) — single point for coordination and timing.
- Escalation Lead (A): Head of Customer Success / Customer Success Director — authorized to negotiate up to X% discount or credits.
- Technical Lead (C): Solutions Engineer — owns urgent technical investigation and mitigation.
- Legal/Sales (C): Sales Ops / Legal — on standby for amended terms or SOWs.
- Exec Sponsor (I/C): VP Customer Success — engaged for exec-level conversations.

Risk indicators matrix (quick):
- Usage drop >40%: high risk
- Open product bugs blocking core flows: high risk
- Billing dispute / invoicing >30 days unresolved: high risk
- Exec sponsor changed or inactive: medium-high
- Integration delays >2 sprints: medium
- Feature roadmap misalignment: medium

Triage checklist (48h):
- Gather signals: product telemetry, API logs, billing records, previous QBR notes, and support tickets (owner: CSM).
- Internal huddle within 24h: CSM + SE + Sales rep + Renewal AE + Escalation Lead. Document blockers and identify top 2 immediate fixes.
- Customer touch: send an empathetic, concise 'we heard you' email and request 30-min alignment call. Use template below.
- Set 72h plan: list of actions owner and ETA; publish to customer and internal stakeholders.

Mitigation plays (pick 1–3, prioritize by impact & speed):
- Hotfix / workaround bundle: SE to deliver a temporary fix or config change that materially restores key flows (goal within 5 business days).
- Usage reactivation campaign: trigger guided sessions, 2 targeted product walkthroughs, and playbooks for end-users to regain value.
- Billing remediation: issue a credit or a payment plan to remove cash friction; coordinate with Finance.
- Implementation rescue: offer a short SOW for focused implementation sprint (2–4 weeks) with dedicated SE time.
- Light-touch concessions: limited-time pricing adjustment or trial extension tied to a commitments plan (must be approved by Escalation Lead).

Executive escalation play (script + agenda):
- When to escalate: no substantive progress after mitigation phase / customer requests exec engagement / contract at risk within 30 days.
- Ask: Escalation Lead to secure 30–45 min exec meeting within 72h.
- Agenda (30 mins): 1) State mutual goal, 2) Top 3 impact areas + current mitigation status, 3) Specific asks from Customer Exec (decision points), 4) Redwood commitments + timeline, 5) Next steps + signatures.
- Script highlights: Be concise, data-led (usage, revenue, business impact), and present a clear single decision with options (e.g., approve rescue SOW / accept credit / extend term conditional on adoption commitments).

Customer email templates (short & editable):
- Initial (triage):
Subject: Quick alignment? Plan to remove friction for <customer-name>
Hi <sponsor>,
We noticed <signal> and want to make this right. Can we schedule a 30-minute sync this week to align on the quickest path to restoring value? I’ll bring our SE and Solutions lead and come prepared with a 72-hour plan.
Thanks,
<CSM>

- Exec request (only after internal approvals):
Subject: Exec check-in: remove renewal friction for <customer-name>
Hi <exec-name>,
We’re seeing a near-term renewal decision and a couple of blockers that need exec alignment. Would you be available for a 30–45 min call this week to decide between the proposed options? Agenda and materials attached.
Best,
<Escalation Lead>

Decision authority and concession guardrails:
- CSM: can approve non-financial remediation (playbooks, training, configurations).
- Escalation Lead: authorized to approve up to 10% credit or one-time service credit; any pricing >10% or long-term term changes require VP approval and Sales Ops sign-off.
- Legal: required sign-off for contract language or T&Cs adjustments.

Negotiation options (simple palette):
- Option A (Value-first): No discount; immediate rescue SOW + adoption milestones; sign within 14 days.
- Option B (Time-limited concession): 6-week credit (X% of monthly invoice) tied to adoption plan + exec check-in at 30 days.
- Option C (Contract amendment): One-time discount >10% or term change — requires VP + Sales Ops sign-off and SOW for adoption remediation.

Escalation artifacts to produce (deliverables):
- 1-page one-pager for execs: impact, options, recommended ask (use the attached template).
- 72-hour action plan (internal + customer view).
- Updated risk register entry and cadence: daily standups until mitigations are closed.

Metrics to track during sprint (minimum):
- Weekly active user count (WAU) and weekly request volume (WQV) on impacted flows.
- Time to first resolution for tickets flagged as blockers.
- Customer engagement: meetings completed, exec response time, adoption sessions delivered.
- Revenue resolution: signed amendment or renewal status change.

Communication cadence (internal + customer):
- Day 0–3: daily internal standups (15 min) and customer-facing status at least twice in the first week.
- Day 4–14: alternate day internal updates, weekly customer updates until closed.
- After close: 30-day follow-up QBR scheduled and documented in Customer Success Plan.

Failure modes and contingency steps:
- If no customer engagement after 3 outreach attempts: escalate to Sales AE and attempt exec email copy; document attempts and prepare for one final outreach with a defined last-offer.
- If technical fix cannot be delivered within 10 business days: propose full rescue SOW and offer temporary operational workaround or rollback to known-good config.
- If customer requests deep concessions beyond guardrails: convene VP-level decision meeting and prepare 1-page economic tradeoff memo.

Quick templates/attachments (placeholders to copy):
- Exec one-pager header: Customer | ARR | Renewal date | Main impact | Proposed option | Recommended ask | Next step
- 72-hour plan table columns (Item | Owner | ETA | Customer impact | Status)

Post-sprint: institutionalize learnings
- Capture root cause (product, implementation, adoption, pricing), update internal playbook entry with signal patterns and new recommended mitigations.
- Create a short case study (internal) if win; if loss, run a 2-week postmortem focused on earliest detection improvements.

Appendix: quick checklist for CSM on day 1
- Verify renewals rep and AE are looped in.
- Pull last 12 months of telemetry + SLA incidents.
- Compile support case list and tag critical blockers.
- Draft the 1-page exec brief (even if not used) to force clarity.

Notes / Open questions (working):
- Define a standard approval matrix for concessions that includes dollar thresholds rather than percent to keep consistency across ARR tiers.
- Consider a small pool of pre-approved SE hours that can be deployed quickly without long SOW cycles for mid-market rescues.

Usage guidance:
- Lightweight: keep documents short and concrete — execs will only read 1 page.
- Use metrics, not emotion. Bring clear single asks.
- Timebox decisions: default to the shortest path that preserves revenue and re-establishes value.

Document history:
- v0.1 (2025-11-05) initial draft by Aisha Patel
- v0.5 (2025-12-08) added negotiation palette and metrics by Diego Ramirez
- v1.0 (2026-02-10) updated guardrails and escalation lead procedures by Mei Chen

End of blueprint.
